nonBlockingNotes: AC1's dead-path-comment removal is well-covered and even improves on the ticket: the design correctly flags the ticket's cited ranges (~525-561 / ~810-833) as stale/live-code per Q9 and re-derives the true residue locations — a defensible, traceable handling of that sub-requirement.

Open Questions OQ1-OQ4 are genuine unresolved design choices (enum vs booleans, AC4 sufficiency, which guide-pack file survives, whether the /review-* collapse is its own slice). These are flagged honestly rather than papered over, so they are not coverage gaps, but a reviser/maintainer must resolve OQ3 (surviving canonical guide) before AC3 can be implemented.

OQ1 (design.md:94) leaves the new field's shape open (`ciCounterAction` enum vs. two booleans) while Slice 2/Decision 1 commit to `ciCounterAction`. This is internally consistent (the open question explicitly flags the name as provisional, and the body uses it as a working name) — noted only so the reviser knows the field name is not yet settled.

All other cross-references in the design resolve cleanly: the `decision()` factory key set matches scripts/qrspi_resolve_state.py, the cap logic (`attempt < ci_revise_cap`, `ciGaveUp`, `load_ci_revise_cap`/`coerce_cap`) matches the resolver and qrspi_resolve.py, the dead-path comment line numbers (48/168/1033/1169/1212) agree between Current State and the Risk Register, the `answered.some(a=>a.applied)` JS-only gate matches doRevise, and every referenced doc/script file (guide-pack, eval-system.md, eval_all.py, canonical lifecycle doc) exists on disk.

AC4 (Slice 2) is the one place the design departs from the ticket's literal wording: the ticket says 'Move the counter state machine (bumpCiReviseTrailers/resetCiReviseTrailer ...) out of doRevise into qrspi_resolve_state.py', but the design re-scopes this to adding a single ciCounterAction verdict field + tests, on the grounds (Q6) that the cap decision already lives in the resolver and (Q2/Q5) the bump/reset WRITE cannot move because the `answered.applied` signal is computed only post-worker in JS. This is a defensible, research-grounded narrowing rather than scope drift, and the design honestly surfaces the residual judgment as OQ2 instead of silently dropping the ticket's 'move the state machine' language. Advisory only: the maintainer should confirm via OQ2 that the verdict-field relocation (not relocating more of the write machinery) is the intended reading of AC4 'the counter logic lives in the resolver'.

The design correctly overrides the ticket's own stale line citations for the dead-path comments (~525-561 / ~810-833) using research Q9, which verified those ranges are live code. Faithful to research over an erroneous ticket detail — noted only so a reviewer is aware the design intentionally contradicts a literal ticket instruction here.

AC4 Decision 1 introduces a NEW `ciCounterAction` enum field whose value is fully derivable from the two booleans the decision dict already carries (`ciFailing`, `changeRequested` — see qrspi-batch.js:1019-1038, where the existing JS branch already dispatches on exactly those two). The added field is justified (the ticket's AC4 explicitly asks JS to stop deriving the verdict, and it extends the existing fixed-key-dict pattern rather than inventing a new mechanism), so this is not a blocking simplicity finding — but the design's own OQ1 (enum vs two booleans) is the right question to resolve, since a two-boolean verdict would add zero new key shapes while still moving the derivation into the tested resolver.

AC3 doc consolidation (Slice 3) bundles three distinct mechanical changes — merge five guide-pack files, dedup the lifecycle narrative across four locations, and collapse four /review-* skills onto a shared loop reference — into one slice; the design itself flags this in OQ4 (whether the /review-* collapse should be its own slice). Splitting is a structure-phase concern, not a simplicity defect in the design, but the bundling is worth the maintainer's attention.

design.md line 12 carries research Q4's claim verbatim ('a grep returns only these five agent-file mentions, no definition or call') — true only when scoped to `qrspi-batch.js`; the design's AC1 silently widened that scope to all of `.claude/` (the source of the blocking finding above). The factual narrative is otherwise accurate.

AC2 / Q11 frame 'six locations' for the eval placeholder wording. Verified against the tree: the literal string 'non-functional placeholder' appears in exactly 5 files (`.claude/CLAUDE.md:187`, `scripts/eval_all.py:11`, `docs/qrspi-orientation.md:76`, `docs/qrspi_quick_reference.md:208`, `docs/qrspi_practical_application.md:185`); `docs/eval-system.md` is the sixth via 'Stub' table wording + the version-pinned `run_eval.py:117-137` / `revise.py:26-44` citations (confirmed at lines 97/101), not that exact literal string. The Slice 3 Delta handles both correctly; only the 'six identical strings' framing is slightly loose.

AC4 architecture (Decisions 1 & 2) is sound and internally coherent against the real `doRevise` (qrspi-batch.js:1019-1038, 956-965): the three counter-write paths are CI-failing->bump (unconditional), green change-request->reset (unconditional), comment-only->reset (gated on the JS-only post-worker `answered.some(a=>a.applied)`). The resolver can correctly own the bump/reset/none verdict for the two pre-worker-determinable paths while Decision 2 properly keeps the `applied` confirmation in JS — verified, no defect. Resolver factory (185-198), step-2c cap (288-303), `ci_revise_attempt_of` max-aggregation (129-138), and the `case(...)` test harness (62-66, 343+) all match the design's claims.

Q8 (per-slice max aggregation of the counter) is treated as already-covered by the existing qrspi_resolve_state_test.py:343-474 suite rather than getting a new RUS-92 test case. This is a defensible reading of AC4 (which only names bump/reset/cap transitions), but if the reviewer expects the new ciCounterAction field asserted under per-slice aggregation, the design's test plan (Slice 2) does not explicitly call that case out.

AC4 is satisfied by a narrowed deliverable (move the bump-vs-reset *verdict* into the resolver via a new field, since the cap decision already lives there). The design is transparent about this and raises it as OQ2 for maintainer confirmation, so the criterion is covered, but final AC4 closure depends on the maintainer agreeing the verdict-field move is 'enough.'

AC2 / Decision 3 count nuance (not a contradiction): the design repeatedly asserts 'all six' eval-doc locations carry the string 'non-functional placeholder' and Slice 3 says 'Correct the six "non-functional placeholder" strings'. In fact only five files contain the literal phrase 'non-functional placeholder' (.claude/CLAUDE.md, scripts/eval_all.py, docs/qrspi_quick_reference.md, docs/qrspi-orientation.md, docs/qrspi_practical_application.md); the sixth, docs/eval-system.md, expresses the same status via a 'Stub' table with version-pinned line citations (lines 97/101) rather than the exact phrase. The design itself acknowledges this distinction in Current State and the Risk Register (it calls out eval-system.md's citations as a separate, citation-verification concern), so the '<count> placeholder strings' phrasing in the AC2/Slice-3 summary is loose shorthand rather than an internal contradiction — but Slice 3's literal 'Correct the six "non-functional placeholder" strings' overstates by one and could mislead a reviser into expecting a sixth literal string in eval-system.md.

Open Question OQ1 and Decision 1 are mutually aware, not contradictory: Decision 1 recommends a single 'ciCounterAction' enum {bump,reset,none}, while OQ1 leaves enum-vs-two-booleans open and notes the existing dict uses boolean verdict fields. This is a deliberately-flagged open choice, not an unresolved internal conflict — the design consistently treats 'ciCounterAction' as the working proposal pending the OQ1 answer.

AC1 acceptance bar relaxed vs. the ticket's literal command: ticket AC1 specifies `grep -rn "runCriticPanelLoop" .claude/` returns zero hits, but the design narrows the bar to `.claude/agents/` so the descriptive contract-shape comments in `.claude/workflows/qrspi-review.js` and `qrspi-teeth-eval.js` may remain. This is a defensible refinement (I verified those workflow-file mentions are accurate live-code documentation, not pivot residue, and AC1's own prose says 'zero hits in agent frontmatter', which contradicts its own command) and the design flags it explicitly rather than silently. Worth surfacing because the literal AC1 command, if used verbatim as the acceptance gate, would still report hits — the structure/plan phase should confirm the maintainer accepts the frontmatter-scoped grep as the AC1 gate.

AC4 is scoped down from the ticket's 'move the CI-Revise-Attempt counter state machine into the resolver' to 'move the bump-vs-reset verdict (new ciCounterAction field) + tests', because research (verified) shows the cap decision already lives in the tested resolver and the trailer write necessarily stays in qrspi_ci_revise_bump.py + the JS post-worker `answered.applied` gate. The design honestly flags this as OQ2 (is moving the verdict sufficient, or does the maintainer expect more write machinery relocated?). Not a drift — it neither over- nor under-reaches given the ground truth — but the open question should be resolved before the plan phase commits to the smaller deliverable.

Decision 1 recommends an enum `ciCounterAction` while OQ1 leaves enum-vs-two-booleans open, citing that the existing dict uses boolean verdict fields. This is a defensible deferred decision (an enum over three mutually-exclusive states is if anything simpler than two booleans), not unjustified complexity — flagged only as an advisory loose end for the maintainer to close.

The added `ciCounterAction` field is justified against AC4's 'JS no longer derives that state' requirement and the pure-core/imperative-shell pattern; it targets the bump-vs-reset write verdict (re-derived in untestable JS today), not the cap decision that research Q3 notes is already encoded by `ciFailing`/`ciGaveUp`. No redundancy concern.

AC2 path-naming slip (Delta Slice 3 / Desired End State AC2 / Risk Register row 5): the design says the docs/eval-system.md line citations (run_eval.py:117-137, revise.py:26-44) must be re-verified 'against the live evals/ tree', but the actual files live in scripts/ (scripts/run_eval.py is 326 lines, scripts/revise.py is 349 lines), not evals/ (which holds only fixtures/golden/teeth/*.json). This is an inherited imprecision from research.md Q11 and is harmless — the edit target docs/eval-system.md is correct and the citations are relative file-name references — but a reviser following the literal 'evals/ tree' instruction would look in the wrong directory.

OQ2 / Decision 1 honestly bounds AC4: the design concedes the cap DECISION already lives in the tested resolver (verified: qrspi_resolve_state.py step 2c at lines 288-307 returns revise/ciFailing under cap and wait/ciFailing/ciGaveUp at cap), so the actual AC4 deliverable is reduced to adding a ciCounterAction verdict field plus tests. This is a defensible reading of the ticket's 'counter logic lives in the resolver' bar, but the design itself flags (OQ2) that the maintainer may expect more write machinery relocated — the scope of AC4 satisfaction is therefore maintainer-dependent, not objectively settled by the design.
